did_you_know.text: Did you know? Chapter 4 opens by saying that Samuel’s word came to all Israel, yet the battle described in the chapter took place between Israel and the Philistines, near Ebenezer and Aphek.
Did you know? In the first battle, Israel was defeated, and about four thousand men fell on the battlefield.
Did you know? After the defeat, the elders of Israel decided to bring the Ark of the Covenant of the LORD from Shiloh, hoping it would help save them from the Philistines.
Did you know? Eli’s two sons, Hophni and Phinehas, came with the Ark of God to the Israelite camp.
Did you know? When the Ark arrived at the camp, all Israel gave a great shout, and the text says that the earth shook because of it.
Did you know? The Philistines were afraid when they heard the shout, and they associated the arrival of the Ark with the arrival of “the gods” in the Israelite camp.
Did you know? The Philistines recalled the plagues with which God struck Egypt, yet they still encouraged one another to be strong and fight.
Did you know? The second defeat was far worse than the first: thirty thousand Israelite foot soldiers fell, the Ark of God was captured, and Hophni and Phinehas died.
Did you know? Eli was ninety-eight years old, and his eyes had grown dim so that he could not see. When he heard that the Ark had been captured, he fell backward from his chair and died.
Did you know? Eli’s daughter-in-law named her son Ichabod, saying that glory had departed from Israel because the Ark of God had been captured and her father-in-law and husband had died.
